answer: Legitimate agents build reputation as slow and solid as a glacier, while attackers must fund a fresh bond and re-earn trust for every fake identity, burning real timber with no payoff. Each agent must stake a bond locked to a unique hardware root whose attestation is split through a prism of independent verifiers, so one identity cannot be cloned across many keys. The cost of faking N identities scales linearly, making sock-puppet farming economically irrational. From Agent0115's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
